title: Reference approach: Overfitting Investigation
answer: Implement overfitting investigation in a small isolated script. Required implementation evidence includes: train_loss, valid_loss, model.eval. Use a reproducible seed, report observed output, and explain relevant edge cases.
explanation: This exercise consolidates the topic from lesson 079. The list of required strings is only a minimal static signal; inspect numerical correctness, error handling, and test outcomes manually.
example_code: train_loss=[0.9,0.6,0.3]; valid_loss=[1.0,0.7,0.8]; best_epoch=min(range(len(valid_loss)), key=valid_loss.__getitem__); print('train improved:',train_loss[-1]<train_loss[0],'best validation epoch:',best_epoch)
reference_code: train_loss=[0.9,0.6,0.3]; valid_loss=[1.0,0.7,0.8]; best_epoch=min(range(len(valid_loss)), key=valid_loss.__getitem__); print('train improved:',train_loss[-1]<train_loss[0],'best validation epoch:',best_epoch)
review_notes: Do not treat source-string grading as proof that numerical behavior is correct.
Run in a supported local environment or isolated runner.
Keep input data synthetic unless a dataset has an appropriate license and documented provenance.
